verdicts.reason: Both put the white 'Lima & Co Group' wordmark on top of the white circle and the busy gold halftone, without its navy panel. Most of the name disappears, and the cropped graphics no longer read as a rearranged layout. A is worse: it swaps in a thin font that drops the brand typeface, and almost every letter is lost ('Group' is only fragments). B keeps the original geometric font at a larger size, so 'Co' reads cleanly on navy, but 'Lima &' and 'Group' are still unreadable against white and halftone.
